A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Video-o3 study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–J support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-QA and temporal-grounding results, component ablations, training curves, efficiency measurements and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds MMR-V results, smaller-model evaluation, additional ablations and resource measurements.

M1.justification: The tool-invocation procedure, TDAM, trajectory-guided reward and data-synthesis pipeline remain unchanged. Section 3.3 now names DAPO, but v1 already specified DAPO in Section 5.1. The Qwen3-VL-4B experiment instantiates the existing framework without documenting a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Table 1 adds MMR-V, extending evaluation to reasoning over implicit visual evidence. Existing video-QA benchmarks, Charades-STA and training-data coverage are retained. VideoReasonBench is newly discussed as a limitation, without reported evaluation.

E2.justification: VideoChat-R1 is added to the main QA comparison and the MLVU efficiency comparison; VideoChat-R1.5 was already present in v1's efficiency analysis. New Table 7 compares Video-o3-4B with Qwen3-VL-4B. Existing comparator membership is otherwise retained.

E3.justification: The reported RL sample count changes from 25,600 to 12,800, without establishing whether experiments were rerun. Table 1 replaces LOVE-R1 and Video-Zoomer entries with explicitly marked reproductions under the same evaluation environment and 16k initial visual quota. New protocols cover a 4B backbone, grounding-data controls, annotation-mixture settings, and resource and turn-count metrics.

E4.justification: New analyses isolate the Hybrid Clue Score with and without grounding data, quantify turn distributions with and without Turn Decay Factor, test sparse trajectory annotations supplemented by free-format data, and assess transfer to a smaller backbone. The existing efficiency analysis is expanded with memory and token measurements. Earlier ablations and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Existing training-curve smoothing and validation-sample reporting are unchanged. New turn-distribution summaries report behavioral outcomes rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds MMR-V scores of 45.3% for RL and 44.7% for SFT+RL, alongside smaller-model, ablation and resource results. Existing 7B Video-o3 benchmark values are retained. Baseline entries change: LOVE-R1's MLVU score moves from 67.4 to 69.9 under the newly documented reproduction setting, which is not a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The attention-mask, reward, quota and over-turn optimization definitions in Equations 1–9 are retained. Added reward explanations do not introduce new mathematical assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims about native tool invocation, TDAM, trajectory-guided rewards and Seeker-173K. Headline MLVU and Video-Holmes accuracies remain 72.1% and 46.5%. Added experiments provide support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning direct localization supervision, practical turn-budget adequacy and learning with sparse trajectory annotations. Section 5.6 qualifies transfer by dependence on the backbone's grounding ability. Appendix J adds the mismatch with abstract puzzle-style reasoning supervision; existing context-length and tool-scalability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies baseline-result provenance and matched initial quotas, aligns the optimization description with the already stated DAPO implementation, and revises the documented RL sample count. Its Impact Statement newly specifies CC-BY sourcing for self-collected videos. Prompts, tool quotas, remaining training details and the project URL are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially refines the novelty comparison: it explicitly acknowledges Conan and VideoZoomer as native multi-turn predecessors and distinguishes Video-o3 through task decoupling and verifiable trajectory rewards. It also expands coverage of keyframe selection and sparse-memory approaches, including KOALA, MovieChat, MDP3 and VideoMiner.

P1.justification: Changes include localized related-work rewriting, expanded reward explanations, new experimental subsections, and moving efficiency analysis from Appendix E.4 into Section 5.5. Conference front matter, acknowledgements and an Impact Statement are added. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially expanded: Table 1 gains a benchmark column, comparator row and reproduction markers; the relocated efficiency table gains memory and token columns; and new Tables 7, 12, 13 and 15 present additional comparisons and analyses. Best-score highlighting is corrected in retained tables. Figures 1–15 retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence supporting the unchanged method. Matched-budget baseline reproductions improve comparison credibility, while the grounding-data-controlled ablation directly tests the reward's contribution to localization. Smaller-model, sparse-annotation and turn-distribution analyses substantiate generalization and efficiency more convincingly than v1. Research positioning also better acknowledges native predecessors. The unexplained RL sample-count revision and continued absence of uncertainty estimates remain limitations, but the added controls materially improve the paper's empirical foundation.
